note: The three 2026-10-30 profiles plus a synthetic pharmacy technician. All invented.

profiles.label: hospital nurse
profiles.job: registered nurse on a medical-surgical unit at a community hospital, 12-hour day shifts
roles: charge nurse a few shifts a month
profiles.goals_freeform: our hospital is rolling out new charting and AI documentation tools and I want to follow what the IT and vendor people are saying in meetings
profiles.background_text: eight years at the bedside. comfortable with the electronic health record, barcode medication administration, shift handoff reports and infusion pumps. no programming background.

profiles.label: retail pharmacist
profiles.job: staff pharmacist at a neighborhood retail pharmacy
profiles.goals_freeform: the pharmacy software keeps changing and I want to understand the technical terms the help desk and software trainers use
profiles.background_text: PharmD, eleven years in community pharmacy. daily work includes prescription verification, drug utilization review, insurance claim adjudication and rejections, prior authorizations, controlled-substance counts and immunizations. no programming background.

profiles.label: high-school teacher
profiles.job: high-school biology teacher at a public high school
roles: sits on the school technology committee
profiles.goals_freeform: students use AI tools constantly and the district is choosing new software; I want to ask good questions on the technology committee
profiles.background_text: fourteen years teaching biology and AP environmental science. uses the school's learning management system and a gradebook daily. writes lab rubrics and unit plans. no programming background.

profiles.label: pharmacy technician (synthetic)

roles: runs the drive-thru window on weekends
profiles.goals_freeform: the pharmacy software keeps changing and I want to follow what the trainers say
